problem_text: Let A be a graded Noetherian ring, with A_0 a field and A generated by A_1. Show that A is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if for all homogeneously prime p, (A_p)_0 is Cohen-Macaulay.
solution_text: Proof outline: (=>) If A is CM, then A_p is CM local for every prime p. For homogeneous prime p, the homogeneous localization (A_p)_0 is a local ring whose depth and dimension match those of A_p (via the structural relationship for standard graded algebras), so (A_p)_0 is CM. (<=) If (A_p)_0 is CM for all homogeneous primes p, then A_p is CM for all homogeneous primes. For standard graded algebras over a field, every prime contains a homogeneous prime with the same CM property (homogeneous spectrum is sufficiently rich), so A_q is CM for all primes q, hence A is CM.
solution_summary: The equivalence follows from two key facts: (1) for standard graded algebras, homogeneous localization (A_p)_0 faithfully reflects the CM property of A_p, and (2) for standard graded algebras over a field, checking CM at homogeneous primes suffices because every prime has an associated homogeneous prime with the same depth and dimension.
answer: A is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if for all homogeneously prime p, (A_p)_0 is Cohen-Macaulay. The proof uses: (=>) CM is preserved under localization and homogeneous localization reflects CM; (<=) for standard graded algebras over a field, checking at homogeneous primes suffices.
